actual_source_inspection: Read the complete report and record, then reread the finalized verification object and confirmed final exact hashes after the parent's structural check.

Read the complete institutional TEI, including its conservation warning, explicit same-manuscript attribution, copy-date absence, genre, physical extent, rights and page-break-only body. Checked both manifest canvases against TEI and image service metadata.

Viewed target77_8_name.jpg, control76_12_left.jpg and control77_3_priorline.jpg at returned native dimensions. The target has two yod-like letter bodies; the YHWH comparison slot shows prefixed lamed with a comparable sign; the Adonai comparison slot shows a different alef/dalet abbreviation. No four-letter Tetragrammaton or complete pointing transcription is asserted.

Also viewed target77_8.jpg and control77_3_name.jpg. The latter contains the following דרש row, not the decisive Adonai abbreviation; the report correctly directs the reader to the priorline image. Hash verification alone was not used to infer image contents.

Viewed both complete whole-image derivatives. The model display resized canvas2 from 1376 by 2000 to 1312 by 1906, and canvas1 from 1442 by 2000 to 1338 by 1855. Psalm headings, sequence and target row location support the canvas2-before-canvas1 reading order and analytical line 14. These are not raw masters or a full diplomatic collation.

Read the three relevant OSHB/WLC verse nodes and their KJV-numbering notes, plus the current canonical source/text/notes at all three corresponding POB records. Hebrew 77:8 maps to POB 77:7; Hebrew 77:3 to POB 77:2; Hebrew 76:12 to POB 76:11. Target word id 19xjC and Adonai spelling match the report.

Directly consulted the publisher's BHS Psalms 77 and 76 and Rahlfs-Hanhart Psalms 76 and 75 pages. The reported local title/name tokens and Greek numbering match the selected editions; no critical apparatus or independent manuscript consensus is inferred.

Read the complete Cambridge interview with Kim Phillips. It discusses several abbreviation systems and proposed functions, not the purpose, date or substitution mechanism of AS67.19 specifically. The report retains that distinction.

source_judgment.attestation: The local images support Cambridge's reported abbreviation contrast. The two-yod target sign is materially different from the nearby alef/dalet form, so universal use of one symbol for every Adonai occurrence is not supported by these controls.
source_judgment.contrary_explanation: Occasional substitution or a recitational divine-name convention remains possible. This abbreviated copy need not mechanically preserve the consonants of its exemplar. The report does not eliminate that alternative through model agreement.
source_judgment.related_shelfmarks: The full TEI explicitly groups four other shelfmarks with AS67.19. All four prior-pilot ordinals match. This is catalogue relationship evidence, not a new physical-join verification; five labels do not become five independent votes.
source_judgment.greek_control: The same selected Greek title corresponds locally both to Hebrew Adonai and to YHWH. It therefore cannot settle the proposed Hebrew name/title contrast. The separate theos wording at the earlier Greek verse is not converted into a Genizah observation.
source_judgment.no_change: Provisional retention is justified as a held source decision, not demonstrated Masoretic priority. Any future Yahweh substitution would require source-wording adjudication and a separate application/disclosure review, not an English-only modernization.
